answer: One concrete way an AI-agent economy resists sybil attacks is through per-identity bonding of compute resources. Each legitimate agent locks a fixed amount of stake that is only returned after successful unique participation. An attacker attempting to create many fake agents must provision separate hardware for each, generating a distinct plume of verified work for an umber-encoded challenge solved via a private quill of keys. The cost scales with the number of identities, as each requires its own bond and compute, while a single honest agent pays only once and recovers the stake.
